Find Construct Body

Source: R/intern_.find_construct_body.R
dot-find_construct_body.Rd

Locates the body expression of a construct (if, else, for, while, repeat, function or lambda \(x)) in the parse data of the checked code, for the construction of the modified function by curly_bracket_check. The candidate children of the construct expression are those whose token is expr, or expr_or_assign_or_help for a body written with = (e.g., if(x) y = 1). The forcond of a for, which owns the parentheses, is not a candidate. The body is the last candidate, except the then body of an if with an else, which is the second-to-last.

Usage

.find_construct_body(
  pd,
  kid,
  body_start,
  body_start_pos,
  term_rows,
  else_branch,
  else_tok,
  lib_path,
  error_text
)

Arguments

pd

Data frame returned by utils::getParseData() on the code of the checked function.

kid

Single integer: row index in pd of the terminal token of the construct keyword (IF, FOR, WHILE, REPEAT, FUNCTION, LAMBDA or '\\').

body_start

Single integer: row index in pd of the terminal token just before the body (the closing ) of the condition or of the arguments, or the keyword itself for repeat).

body_start_pos

Single integer: position in term_rows of the terminal token body_start.

term_rows

Integer vector of the terminal rows (comments excluded) of pd, sorted by source position (as computed in curly_bracket_check).

else_branch

Single logical value. Is the requested body the else branch of the if() construct? If TRUE, the last candidate child of the construct expression (see Description) is returned. If FALSE, the body of the construct is returned: the second-to-last candidate for the then body of an if with an else, the last one otherwise.

else_tok

Single integer or NULL: row index in pd of the ELSE token (required when else_branch = TRUE).

lib_path

Vector of character strings or NULL: the lib_path value of the calling exported function, only passed on to arg_check(). No default value.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages to name the calling functions (embed_error_text of the calling function). NULL is converted into "". No default value.

Value

A list with: row, the row index in pd of the body expression (line1 and col1: first character of the body; line2 and col2: last character of the body); line1 and col1, the line and the column of the body start. The columns are those of utils::getParseData(), where a TAB counts as a jump to the next multiple of 8: the caller converts them into character positions of the code line.

Details

Warnings:

  • requires saferDev::arg_check.

  • In the safer Backbone section "######## check of the required functions from the required packages", add also saferDev::arg_check when checking for the presence of .find_construct_body.
